title: Verify that rigid motions take parallel lines to parallel lines

sections.skill: Verify that rigid motions take parallel lines to parallel lines

questions.skill: Verify that rigid motions take parallel lines to parallel lines
questions.prompt: The parallel lines y = 2x and y = 2x + 3 are reflected across the x-axis. Write the equations of the images and check whether the images are parallel.
questions.prompt_markup:
The parallel lines y = 2x and y = 2x + 3 are reflected across the x-axis.
Write the equations of the images and check whether the images are parallel.
questions.correct_answer: y = -2x and y = -2x - 3; both have slope -2 (and different y-intercepts), so the images are parallel.
questions.grading_note: Grade both: the two equations and the slope check.

questions.skill: Verify that rigid motions take parallel lines to parallel lines
questions.response: draw on the figure and write an answer
questions.prompt: The two segments are parallel. Translate both segments 4 units to the left and draw the images. Then find the slope of each image and compare.
questions.prompt_markup: The two segments are parallel. Translate both segments 4 units to the left and draw the images. Then find the slope of each image and compare.
questions.correct_answer: Both images have slope 2/3, so they are still parallel.
questions.drawing_answer: Segments from (-3, 1) to (0, 3) and from (-3, -2) to (0, 0)
questions.grading_note: Grade both: the two image segments, and the two equal slopes.

figure.description: Coordinate grid with x from -6 to 6 and y from -6 to 6. Straight line through (1, 1) and (4, 3). Straight line through (1, -2) and (4, 0).

questions.skill: Verify that rigid motions take parallel lines to parallel lines
questions.prompt: The line y = 2x + 1 is translated 3 units up. What is the equation of the image? Is the image parallel to the original line?
questions.prompt_markup:
The line y = 2x + 1 is translated 3 units up.
What is the equation of the image? Is the image parallel to the original line?
questions.correct_answer: y = 2x + 4; yes, the slope is still 2.

questions.skill: Verify that rigid motions take parallel lines to parallel lines

questions.skill: Prove theorems about angles formed by parallel lines
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: In the figure, lines m and n are parallel. Prove that angle 2 = angle 7. Give a reason for each step.
questions.prompt_markup: In the figure, lines m and n are parallel. Prove that angle 2 = angle 7. Give a reason for each step.
questions.required_method: A valid chain of reasons. Other valid orders are accepted. A conclusion without reasons is not full credit. Example: angle 2 = angle 6 (corresponding angles, m ∥ n); angle 6 = angle 7 (vertical angles); so angle 2 = angle 7.

figure.description: Parallel lines m (top) and n (bottom) are cut by transversal t, which slants up to the right. At line n the angles are numbered 1 (above, left of t), 2 (above, right of t), 3 (below, left of t), and 4 (below, right of t). At line m the angles are numbered 5, 6, 7, and 8 in the same positions.

questions.domain: Geometry: Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations
questions.skill: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 10 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: Show that the quadrilateral with vertices (0, 0), (4, 0), (5, 3), and (1, 3) is a parallelogram.
questions.prompt_markup: Show that the quadrilateral with vertices (0, 0), (4, 0), (5, 3), and (1, 3) is a parallelogram.
questions.correct_answer: The sides from (0, 0) to (4, 0) and from (1, 3) to (5, 3) both have slope 0; the sides from (0, 0) to (1, 3) and from (4, 0) to (5, 3) both have slope 3. Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.
